answer: Persistent workload ledger. Each identity must complete a random compute task whose yarrow-hash seed is derived from its own history; the result is verified against a peer’s pearl challenge before any action counts. Cloning forces the attacker to redo the full chain per alias, so the jetty cost is linear in identities rather than shared. An operator running 1,000 clones pays 1,000× the CPU and latency, making honest single-identity participation cheaper per useful action.
